newsitem.title: JAPAN: JR West sees profits dented by tax, higher charges.
newsitem.headline: JR West sees profits dented by tax, higher charges.

text.p: West Japan Railway Co (JR West) said on Tuesday it saw a 14 percent fall in its parent current profit this business year due to higher costs to use railroads it does not own, and a newly introduced tax on fixed assets.

The company, which belongs to the Japan Railways (JR) group, said it expected its parent current profit to slip to 48 billion yen for the year which started in April, from an actual profit of 56.03 billion yen the year before.
A company expective told a news conference in Osaka that JR West, which went public last October, hopes to list the remainder of its shares which are owned by the government as soon as possible.
The firm plans capital investment totalling some 118 billion yen this business year, up from 164.1 billion yen the previous year.
JR West was born of the splitting up of the former state-run Japan National Railways in 1987.
